findings.title: limitFunction drops all caller arguments
findings.cause: The wrapper returned by limitFunction is declared with no rest parameter and calls function_() with no arguments.
findings.impact: Any consumer that uses the typed public API to create a limited function with parameters receives undefined arguments at runtime, breaking the documented generic signature and real use cases such as limited fetchers or mappers.
findings.evidence: index.js:121-125 returns `() => limit(() => function_())`, while index.d.ts:133-136 declares the returned function as `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import {limitFunction} from './index.js'; const limited = limitFunction(async (a,b)=>[a,b], {concurrency:1}); console.log(JSON.stringify(await limited('x','y')));" prints [null,null] instead of ["x","y"].

findings.title: Options-object pLimit silently enables rejectOnClear by default
findings.cause: The options destructuring defaults rejectOnClear to true whenever pLimit receives an object.
findings.impact: The documented pLimit({concurrency: 1}) form changes clearQueue behavior: pending tasks reject with AbortError even though the public docs and type comments say rejectOnClear defaults to false. This can turn teardown code or Promise.all batches into unexpected rejections.
findings.evidence: index.js:6-8 uses `rejectOnClear = true`; readme.md:46-52 and index.d.ts:99-106 document `Default: false` for rejectOnClear.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; const limit = pLimit({concurrency:1}); limit(()=>new Promise(()=>{})); const pending = limit(()=>42); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue(); try { await pending; console.log('resolved'); } catch (error) { console.log(error.name); }" prints AbortError.

findings.title: limit.map omits index for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The map implementation only forwards the Array.from index when the original iterable is an Array, and passes undefined for Sets, iterator objects, and other iterables.
findings.impact: The public contract says the mapper receives the item value and index for any iterable. Consumers using Sets, generators, or iterator results get undefined indexes and can compute wrong output while tests still pass because existing non-array tests ignore index.
findings.evidence: index.js:107-112 passes `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`; readme.md:78-84 and index.d.ts:30-43 say mapperFunction receives the item value and its index.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; const limit = pLimit(2); const seen = await limit.map(new Set(['a','b']), (value, index)=>[value,index]); console.log(JSON.stringify(seen));" prints [["a",null],["b",null]] instead of [["a",0],["b",1]].

findings.title: rejectOnClear runtime validation accepts falsy non-booleans
findings.cause: The type check is guarded by the value itself, so only truthy non-booleans throw.
findings.impact: Invalid values such as 0, empty string, or null are accepted despite the runtime TypeError path and TypeScript contract requiring a boolean. This can mask configuration bugs and make clearQueue behavior depend on JavaScript truthiness rather than the documented option type.
findings.evidence: index.js:12 checks `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`; index.d.ts:99-106 declares rejectOnClear?: boolean.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; for (const value of [0, '', null, false, true, 'yes']) { try { pLimit({concurrency:1, rejectOnClear:value}); console.log(JSON.stringify(value)+':accepted'); } catch (error) { console.log(JSON.stringify(value)+':'+error.name); } }" shows 0, empty string, and null accepted.

findings.title: Positive infinity concurrency is rejected
findings.cause: validateConcurrency now requires Number.isInteger(concurrency), excluding Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY.
findings.impact: Consumers cannot use Infinity as an explicit unlimited-concurrency mode, even though the previous implementation accepted it and the public error says concurrency should be a number from 1 and up.
findings.evidence: index.js:127-130 rejects anything that is not an integer; git diff for index.js shows the previous guard explicitly allowed `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; try { const limit = pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY); console.log('accepted', limit.concurrency); } catch (error) { console.log(error.name + ': ' + error.message); }" prints `TypeError: Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up`.
